title: Cryopreservative Bioink Enables Direct Bioprinting of Adherent Cells.
cell_types: passage-5 human umbilical-cord mesenchymal stromal cells
study_design: Primary biphasic bioink comparison with ice-grain measurements, post-thaw cell outcomes and FAK-inhibitor perturbation
interventions: CAMP: concave HA/collagen microcarriers embedded in oxidized/methacrylated alginate and gelatin matrix

experiments.storage: Three days in liquid nitrogen for the reported cell experiments
experiments.sample_size: Biological donor/assay replicate count not established from the inspected passages
experiments.comparator: DPBS, 10% DMSO/90% FBS, and CAMP + 10% DMSO
experiments.warming: Ice assay anneal −6 °C; grain-size assessment through 30 minutes
experiments.outcome_name: Mean large grain size during recrystallization
experiments.result: Reported MLGS was 91.01 ± 9.3 µm for DPBS, 61.54 ± 3.3 µm for 10% DMSO/90% FBS, 18.73 ± 1.6 µm for CAMP + 10% DMSO, and 21 ± 2.6 µm for CAMP. This is an ice-grain endpoint, not a cell-recovery metric.

experiments.model: P5 human umbilical-cord MSCs, with separate HUVEC/C2C12 checks
experiments.storage: Three days in liquid nitrogen for the reported cell experiments
experiments.sample_size: Biological donor/assay replicate count not established from the inspected passages
experiments.intervention: DMSO-free CAMP after four-day microcarrier culture and matrix encapsulation
experiments.comparator: CAMP with 5% or 10% DMSO and unloading controls; unprotected microcarriers/cell-ink contexts
experiments.cooling: Approximately 300 µL cryovial fill, gel at 4 °C for 20 minutes then transfer to liquid nitrogen; measured cooling rate not reported
experiments.warming: 37 °C thaw; printing at 4–8 °C is a separate subsequent step
experiments.outcome_name: Post-thaw live/dead viability and retained adhesion
experiments.timepoint: Figure 3d/e: three-day storage followed by four-day culture; other panels use different days
experiments.result: Adding 10% DMSO did not significantly improve the reported viability fraction (0.69 ± 0.09 versus 0.64 ± 0.07 without DMSO). Omitting DMSO unloading harmed viability. CAMP retained adhesion and showed protection in multiple cell models, without establishing equivalence or absolute viable-cell yield.

experiments.storage: Three days in liquid nitrogen for the reported cell experiments
experiments.sample_size: Biological donor/assay replicate count not established from the inspected passages
experiments.intervention: 3 µM PF-573228 FAK inhibitor for 24 h before cryopreservation
experiments.cooling: Same CAMP cryopreservation context; no physical-damage-matched inhibitor control established here
experiments.result: The reported viability fraction decreased from 0.68 ± 0.02 to 0.47 ± 0.10 with FAK inhibition. p-FAK localization and reduced p-JNK support pathway involvement; direct target binding or selective downstream causality is not established.
experiments.source_locator: Results 2.4, Figure 4 and Figure S14 discussion; Methods 4.5
experiments.evidence_excerpt: when an inhibitor was used to suppress FAK

main_finding: CAMP combines extracellular ice control with adhesion-associated protection in an MSC bioink. FAK inhibitor treatment reduced post-thaw viability, but this does not establish a dual-action small molecule or broad iPSC efficacy.
limitations: A multicomponent biomaterial system in MSCs/HUVECs/C2C12, not direct iPSC evidence or a small-molecule CPA.
Cryostorage in the inspected cell experiments was three days; three-month bone repair is a later animal endpoint, not three-month storage validation.
Viability/live-dead fractions do not establish absolute recovered viable-cell yield. Donor identities and biological replicate independence are not established from these passages.
Main text says three-day post-thaw culture in one passage; Figure 3 labels four/seven-day readouts. Preserve panel-specific timing rather than assuming a single assay day.
Abstract describes roughly tenfold IRI improvement; the reported mean large grain sizes (91.01 versus 21 µm) are a different explicit endpoint and do not numerically define a tenfold ratio.
Figure 4 caption calls some data ATAC-seq accessible peaks while results discuss differentially expressed genes; assay/contrast mapping and raw data need clarification before omics reanalysis.
FAK-inhibitor perturbation supports pathway involvement, but specificity, general toxicity and physical-damage-matched controls remain needed to isolate the biological contribution.
mechanism_claim: Physical ice-grain measurements and FAK-inhibitor perturbation provide distinct evidence axes. Preserved adhesion/p-FAK and lower p-JNK support a candidate signaling route; they do not prove direct gel-target binding or a drug-like mechanism.
reviewer: Luna source retrieval; root primary methods/results and mechanism-control review

title: Ethylene Glycol and Trehalose Cryopreservation of Cell-Laden Hydrogel Microspheres Enabled by Microfluidic Fabrication.
study_design: Primary microfluidic fabrication and cryopreservation comparison in GelMA and alginate cell-laden microspheres.
supplementary_locators: data/raw/phase4/acs-biomac-5c00559-si.pdf pp. 6-8 (Figures S5-S8): single-agent and EG/trehalose dose series; p. 9 (Figure S9): E/T-D/E/T-G versus D/F-D/D/F-G across GES, U251, A549, HepG2, 3T6, iPSCs; pp. 10-11 (Figures S10-S12): iPSC microsphere viability, caspase-3, and TUNEL.

experiments.model: Multiple cell suspensions and iPSC-laden alginate microspheres; distinguish formulation screen from encapsulated-cell tests
experiments.comparator: 10% v/v DMSO + 10% v/v FBS, with direct and gradient freezing labels
experiments.cooling: Supplement labels direct versus gradient freezing; exact thermal schedules not supplied
experiments.result: E/T maintained >90% post-thaw viability in several cell types and >80% in iPSCs according to the abstract.
experiments.sample_size: Supplement S8: n=3 U251/GES experiments; iPSC donor/replicate count not established
experiments.source_locator: Main abstract for >90%/>80% outcomes; supplementary Figure S9 (PDF pp. 8–9) for formulation units and labels

experiments.comparator: 10% v/v DMSO + 10% v/v FBS, with direct and gradient freezing labels
experiments.outcome_name: CPA-exposure caspase-3 and post-freeze TUNEL signals
experiments.result: Supplement Figure S11 shows higher caspase-3 signal after D/F incubation than E/T or untreated conditions; Figure S12 shows higher TUNEL signal after D/F direct/gradient freezing than E/T or nonfrozen controls. These are distinct exposure and freezing experiments. The main abstract additionally reports preserved pluripotency; no direct apoptosis-target binding is established.
experiments.sample_size: iPSC donor/replicate counts not specified in inspected S11/S12 captions
experiments.source_locator: Supplement Figures S10–S12, PDF pp. 10–11; main abstract for pluripotency

experiments.model: U251 and iPSC-laden alginate microspheres with varied preculture duration
experiments.intervention: Different preculture durations and cluster sizes before freezing
experiments.cooling: Supplement labels direct versus gradient freezing; exact thermal schedules not supplied
experiments.timepoint: Six- and nine-day preculture panels with subsequent post-thaw observation; panel-specific days
experiments.result: Figure S14 reports lower post-thaw viability with larger cell clusters/longer preculture. No exact effect size is digitized here. This adds a negative culture-state constraint to an otherwise favorable formulation screen.
experiments.sample_size: Replicate/donor counts not established from the inspected caption

main_finding: The abstract plus Supplementary Figures S5-S14 support a defined 12% (v/v) ethylene glycol + 4% (w/v) trehalose formulation, direct versus gradient freezing controls, multiple cell lines, and iPSC microsphere viability/pluripotency outcomes.
limitations: Main article remains unavailable. Public supplement confirms formulation units and comparison labels but supplies no complete loading, cooling/warming-rate or storage schedule.
Supplement Figures S5–S8 state n=3 independent experiments for U251/GES assays; this cannot be assigned to every iPSC panel or interpreted as three donors.
Caspase-3 Figure S11 concerns CPA incubation; TUNEL Figure S12 concerns cryopreservation. Do not merge these treatment stages.
Post-thaw live/dead fraction, pluripotency markers and colony formation are distinct outcomes, not an absolute recovered-cell yield.
Figure S14 links increasing preculture/cluster size to poorer cryoprotection, while Figure S2 reports photoinitiator/crosslinking-associated iPSC injury; carrier and culture-state effects matter.
mechanism_claim: Combined CPA/ice and matrix effects are plausible; apoptosis wording is an observed comparison and not proof of direct pathway inhibition.
reviewer: Luna retrieval; root supplementary captions and visual Figures S11/S12 review
